title: AetherLogic integration discovery — edge adapter, LlamaIndex & SDK
action_items: Maya Chen - send SDK sample repo and LangChain/LlamaIndex quickstart by 2028-03-24
Diego Alvarez - prepare rough dedicated pool cost estimate and latency runbook by 2028-03-26
Tom Becker (AetherLogic) - share current API gateway config and rate-limit policy by 2028-03-24
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Solutions), Samir (AetherLogic Platform Lead), Renee (ML Eng), Tom (Security/Infra), Jia (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
AetherLogic evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted + private inference. Primary concerns: integration path with our gateway and LangChain/LlamaIndex stacks, rate-limiting and quota handling for multi-tenant workloads, observability hooks into their Prometheus/Grafana stack, and security posture (SSO/KMS/SOC2). They want a POC with a small dedicated pool and proxy-sidecar that preserves internal auth and enforces token quotas. Redwood to send SDK samples and security docs, schedule POC kick-off next week.

Topics detected: integration approach, SDKs & LangChain adapters, proxy vs sidecar, rate limits/quotas, telemetry & traces, hosted vs dedicated vs private, security controls.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE, Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call — we got Samir, Renee, Tom, Jia from AetherLogic?
[00:04] Samir (AetherLogic): Yep, that's right. Morning/afternoon all.
[00:06] Diego (SE, Redwood): Hi folks, Diego here — I'll focus a bit on the infra details, and Priya will chime on observability and onboarding.
[00:12] Jia (AetherLogic/Product): Great, we have about 45 minutes, want to make sure we cover integration path and security first.
[00:17] Maya: Perfect. Samir, can you give a 2-min on your current stack and what you're trying to achieve?
[00:21] Samir: Sure. We're a B2B analytics platform, multi-tenant. We have an API gateway stack running Envoy + Kong for edge routing. Our ML infra is Kubernetes on AWS EKS, some Triton hosts for heavy model ops, but most prototypes use LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented generation and LangChain for orchestration. We want to add a production LLM layer for customer-facing features — snippet generation, summarization, and some chatops — and we need predictable latency and per-tenant rate limiting. Also data residency for a couple EU customers.
[00:45] Maya: Thanks. Sounds familiar. A few quick clarifying q's — is there an SSO/SAML provider in place for your internal console? And do you want all inference traffic to stay inside VPC for the PII/contracted customers?
[00:54] Tom (Security): Yes, we have Okta SSO for console and internal tooling. For the high-security tenants we need traffic to be within our VPC or on-prem — so Private deployment looks relevant, but we want to evaluate Hosted first for speed.
[01:05] Renee (ML Eng): Also to add: our LlamaIndex pipelines call into a few different LM endpoints now — if we move to Redwood we want minimal code changes. We use their Python SDK and some custom retriever components.
[01:14] Diego: Good to know. We have a few integration patterns: direct SDK from application -> Redwood hosted API; a gateway-side proxy that rewrites auth and enforces quotas; and a sidecar/edge adapter pattern that you can attach to each pod. For LlamaIndex and LangChain, we maintain adapters and quickstarts — often it's a 10-30 line change to swap endpoints and auth.
[01:33] Jia: When you say "adapters" — are those maintained upstream or do we fork? How opinionated are they?
[01:38] Priya (Solutions): We keep canonical adapters in our SDK repo and maintain sample LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors. They're intentionally lightweight. For more bespoke retrievers, customers typically extend them. We can open a PR-based quickstart so your engineers can iterate.
[01:50] Samir: Nice. Rate limiting is a big one — we currently implement per-tenant token quotas at the gateway layer. How does Redwood expose rate/quota controls so we can map our tenant ids?
[01:59] Diego: Two options. If you go through the gateway-side proxy you can inject tenant metadata (x-tenant-id header) and Redwood supports per-API-key and per-tenant policies. For Dedicated or Private, we also allow tokens to be mapped to org IDs and expose quota metrics. You can set hard token caps and soft warnings.
[02:15] Tom: Is header forwarding safe? We're worried about header spoofing at the edge.
[02:18] Diego: We recommend signed tokens from your gateway to Redwood — HMAC-signed metadata or mTLS between the adapters. That prevents spoofing. For Private deployments you can require mutual TLS inside the VPC.
[02:28] Renee: Let's talk latency and batching. Our pipelines are sensitive — typical LlamaIndex calls are 512 tokens generation with top-p sampling, maybe 200ms target. Can Redwood meet that on Hosted vs Dedicated?
[02:38] Diego: For short sequences, Hosted can hit low 100s ms with optimized kernels and our continuous batching disabled for those routes. Dedicated will give you more predictable p99 since you own the pool. For tight latency SLOs we usually recommend a small Dedicated pool pinned to the model variant with a canary rollout.
[02:50] Maya: Also cost tradeoffs — Dedicated has commit costs but gives predictable unit price. Hosted is lower upfront but can spike. Diego will send a cost sketch.
[02:57] Samir: Can you do model variants? We use open models and quantized variants for cost.
[03:00] Diego: Yes, we can host model variants and offer automatic fallbacks if the preferred variant is saturated. The runtime will route by policy (latency, cost).
[03:07] Jia: Observability — can we hook Redwood traces into our Grafana/Tempo/Prometheus stack? We need request-level tracing and token-level cost breakdown in our dashboards.
[03:15] Priya: We export metrics to Prometheus (scrapable endpoint or push gateway) and support OpenTelemetry traces that you can ingest into Tempo/Jaeger. For hosted customers we provide a tracing webhook and raw event stream into S3 if you want raw logs.
[03:29] Renee: Do you provide spans for KV cache hits vs compute? We want to see when retrieval saved tokens.
[03:33] Priya: Yes — we annotate spans for cache/hit/miss, routing decisions, and model variant selection. The token cost per request is returned in the API response and emitted as a metric.
[03:44] Tom: On compliance — SOC2 & encryption keys — can Redwood use our KMS/HSM?
[03:49] Maya: For Private or Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and HSM integrations. For Hosted we manage keys but can offer dedicated encryption domains for enterprise. We'll send the SOC2 pack and KMS integration guide.
[03:59] Samir: What about deployment model for EU data residency? Can we pin to a region?
[04:02] Diego: Yes, region pinning and geo-fencing are supported. Private deployment inside your VPC is most strict; hosted can be pinned to our EU region with contractual assurances.
[04:12] Jia: A practical question: for our LangChain orchestrator, we sometimes batch multiple retrievers into a single LM call. Does Redwood support multi-input batching or do we need to stitch on our side?
[04:21] Diego: We support request multiplexing on the runtime side for compatible payloads, but orchestration patterns that require specific ordering or tool-calling are usually handled at the application layer. We'll share a pattern doc for LangChain multi-retriever flows.
[04:33] Renee: Example: we want to keep cost low so we'd like kv-cache at prefix-level; how does that interact with LlamaIndex embeddings pipeline?
[04:41] Priya: You can use our prefix caching to cache shared prompts and KV cache for autoregressive flows. For embeddings-based retrieval, caching is complementary — you can cache embedding vectors or retrieval results; we have examples in the repo.
[04:52] Samir: Ok, let's drill briefly on the proxy/sidecar approaches — which do you recommend for our Envoy/Kong gateway + EKS setup?
[05:00] Diego: If you want centralized tenant enforcement and minimal app changes, a gateway-side proxy that rewrites auth and injects tenant headers is easiest. If you need per-pod observability and want to enforce quotas locally, a sidecar adapter is better. Sidecar adds a small footprint but gives per-pod telemetry.
[05:13] Tom: Sidecar + mTLS sounds good for high-security tenants. Concern is extra operational surface.
[05:18] Diego: Totally — we can provide Helm charts and a lightweight sidecar image. We also integrate with your CI to do canary rollouts.
[05:25] Jia: Any known friction with LlamaIndex connectors? We had to patch a connector for timeouts before.
[05:30] Priya: We keep an official LlamaIndex connector but customers sometimes tune timeouts and chunking params. We'll give you a tuned quickstart with sensible defaults for RAG latencies.
[05:40] Samir: Demo request: can we run a small POC with 3 tenants, one EU-restricted, one high-security, one default, and test quota enforcement + fallsbacks?
[05:47] Maya: Absolutely. Typical POC is 2-4 weeks: initial integration, baseline latency tests, and a policy validation run. We'll propose a scope in the follow-up note.
[05:56] Tom: On legal/procurement — any standard addenda for private deployments?
[06:00] Maya: We have an enterprise addendum that covers data residency, on-prem private deployment terms, and SLAs. We'll attach that.
[06:05] Renee: For the POC, can you provide a sample cost model? We need to budget for Dedicated pool minimums.
[06:10] Diego: Yes — I'll send a rough monthly estimate for a 2-node dedicated pool with expected token throughput and p50/p95 latency ranges.
[06:16] Jia: Quick question from product: can Redwood emit user-visible explainability metadata back to our app (e.g., which retriever fired, retrieval score)?
[06:24] Priya: We can annotate response payloads with retrieval ids and scores; those fields are configurable and you can redact if needed for customers.
[06:31] Samir: Nice. Any blockers from your side for us to start the POC? We're ready to share gateway config and open a sandbox account.
[06:38] Maya: From Redwood side we'll need a few things: your gateway example config, sample tenant auth flow, and a small prompt set for evals. We'll set up a trial account and provision a dedicated pool window.
[06:48] Tom: We'll share the gateway config by Friday.
[06:50] Maya: Cool. Let's recap next steps.
[06:52] Priya: Recap: Redwood to send SDK + LangChain/LlamaIndex quickstart, SOC2 + KMS guide, cost sketch, and POC scope. AetherLogic to send gateway config and tenant matrix. Schedule POC kickoff for week of 3/27.
[07:05] Samir: Sounds good. Any final Qs?
[07:08] Renee: No, thanks — excited to try the quickstart.
[07:10] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[07:12] Maya: We'll follow up via email with links and action items. Thanks all.

End of transcript (note: timestamps approximate and may drift).
